start.speaker: Brother Cass
start.text: Cass is trimming a wick that does not need trimming, which is what he does instead of looking at the gates.

choices.text: You count what walks past them.

lamps.speaker: Brother Cass
lamps.text: Somebody has to. Not for the light. So that when a thing comes up the stair it has to come up through something that was already here.

count.speaker: Brother Cass
count.text: Eleven this week. I write them in the margin of a book about bees. The book does not mind and neither do I.

quest.speaker: Brother Cass
quest.text: Twelve of them, then, and quietly. The hour between the last lamp and the first is mine, and I would like it back.

rite_offer.speaker: Brother Cass
rite_offer.text:
I know. I lit hers anyway.

There is a rite. It is not a good one and it is not mine to give twice. Say the word and I will say the rest of it.

rite_done.speaker: Brother Cass
rite_done.text:
Then she is owed a walk back up, and the tower is owed nothing at all.

Go and stand where the gates are. She will be there before you are.

rite_declined.speaker: Brother Cass
rite_declined.text: That is also an answer. I will keep the wick trimmed in case you change it.
